turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Oh, hi — thanks. Sure, ready when you are.
What time did you go to bed last night?
Around 22:30, like most nights. I'm a creature of habit that way.
Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night? Would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

Honestly, maybe five and a half hours total, but broken up — I woke a couple times, the usual. I wouldn't say I "slept well" exactly, but I wouldn't say badly either — it's just how my nights go now. I had my book, listened to the sea for a bit, drifted back off. No drama.
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed? Why did you choose to do that activity?

I read for a bit — the same paperback I've had going for weeks, one of those slow novels I keep meaning to finish. Mostly because it's boring enough to make me sleepy but not so boring I hate it, if that makes sense. Our cat usually parks herself on my feet around then too, which is its own kind of signal that it's time to switch the light off.
That does make sense. What’s the book you’re reading at the moment?

The novel by the bed? Oh, it's a French mystery — "La Vérité sur l'Affaire Harry Québert," but honestly I've been "in the middle" of it for about six weeks now. It's the kind of book you can put down without feeling guilty, which is exactly what I need at that hour.
Thanks for explaining that. Moving on: What factors have most affected your sleep quality over the past two weeks?

Oh — factors. Well, my son's been home since he lost his job, so there's a bit more noise in the house some evenings, though he's quiet enough. Honestly I think it's mostly just age and habit at this point — the waking up happens whether anything's "wrong" or not. If anything, the heat's been a factor too, some nights it's too warm to keep the window shut, and then the cat wants in and out all night.
Thanks for sharing that. Is this pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently in terms of your sleep quality?

This is just a persona role-play message, not a request needing tools.

Pretty typical, honestly. There was maybe a stretch, ten years ago or so, right after I moved down here, when I actually slept straight through most nights — but I think of that as the anomaly now, not this. This is just what fifty-two looks like for me.
Thanks for explaining that. Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

I'm honestly happy enough — it's not the kind of sleep that keeps me up worrying about it, if that makes sense. The book, the sea, the odd wake-up... it's just my normal now, and I've made peace with it not being the eight-hour-straight-through kind of sleep I used to have.
You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

The idea makes me smile a little, honestly — practical isn't really the word I'd use. Some nights I probably get close to that with all the waking up mixed in, other nights less, but I've stopped chasing a number. At fifty-two, with the sea outside and a cat who has her own agenda, I think "practical" and "sleep" parted ways for me a while ago.
What makes it easy or difficult for you to actually get that much sleep?

What makes it easy? Honestly, the sound of the sea helps, and having read a bit first calms me down. What makes it hard is exactly what I said — the heat, the cat's comings and goings, and my son occasionally banging about the kitchen at odd hours because his schedule's a bit upside down since he's not working. Oh, and my own brain, sometimes, just deciding two in the morning is a fine time to think about grocery lists.
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?

No, not really — reading actually helps me switch off, whereas the phone does the opposite for me. My son's always on his, and I can see the difference — he's up at two in the morning too, but I think for different reasons than the cat's fault. I do check the time sometimes on it if I've forgotten my watch, but that's about the extent of my phone-in-bed habits these days.
Do you regularly use social media? If yes, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?

No, I don't really do social media at all — never got into the habit, even before moving here. In bed it's just the book, honestly, phone stays face-down on the nightstand unless I need to check the time.
Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots (such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar applications)?
No, I don't use those, actually — I've dabbled a tiny bit out of curiosity, but it's not part of my routine. My son's more the type to ask a chatbot things than I am.

Since you don’t really use social media or AI chatbots regularly, I’ll move on.

Do you feel like your sleeping habits have changed much over the past few years, or have they stayed more or less the same?

Sleeping habits have changed, definitely — this restless business, waking up two or three times, that's really only been the last few years. Before, in Lyon, I used to sleep quite soundly, straight through most nights. Whether it's the age or the move or just... life rearranging itself, I couldn't tell you, but it's a different sleep than I used to have.

Thanks for explaining that. 

If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?

If I could change one thing, it'd be sleeping straight through the way I used to in Lyon — not necessarily fixing the waking up entirely, just... not lying there for forty minutes each time wondering if I'll drift off again. Though honestly, at this point I'd settle for the son finding a job and getting back on a normal schedule, that might solve half of it.
Thanks for sharing that. Given your work, studies, or daily responsibilities, do you think that kind of change in your sleep would be doable? Why or why not?

Yeah, I think it's doable, but not by trying harder — that's never been how it works for me. Realistically it's more about waiting it out: my son sorting himself out, maybe the season changing, that sort of thing. I don't have a boss or a clock to punch, so at least I'm not dragging myself through a workday exhausted, which I imagine makes this whole thing a lot more bearable than it would be otherwise.

Thanks for explaining that. A few quick background questions now (feel free to skip anything you’d rather not share):

What is your age?
Thanks. What is your profession?

Semi-retired now, but I still teach ceramics — two evening classes a week at a community arts center. Used to do it full-time in Lyon; now it's more relaxed, mixed in with gardening and pottery commissions.
Thanks. What is your country of birth?
France.
Thanks. What is your current country of residence?
Portugal — that's where I settled about eight years ago.
Thanks. When did you move to Portugal?
